deck: DIRECT MEDICAL COURIER CONTRACTS, SPECIMEN AND COLD-CHAIN ROUTES, AND THE SPREAD BETWEEN $10 DRIVER STOPS AND $20 TO $50 CLIENT BILLING
NEMT STARTUP ROADMAPS, MEDICAID BROKER WORK, FACILITY REFERRAL PIPELINES, RATES AND BILLING, AND DISPATCH SOFTWARE WITH TRIP VERIFICATION
site_ui.lead: Practitioners show how to land the contract before buying the vehicle, carry HIPAA and bloodborne pathogen training, and win direct lab, pharmacy, medical supply and VA courier work instead of taking brokered runs booked at triple the driver's pay.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies covering medical courier launches, direct contracts, specialized specimen work, NEMT operations, broker relationships, billing and dispatch enforcement. Every claim, metric, pro-tip and quote carries timestamped inline attribution to the practitioner and video it came from.

flow: Complete HIPAA and bloodborne pathogen training and launch in the car you already own, with no van or Sprinter purchase until a signed contract covers the payment.
Ask each client whether it requires a $300,000 or $1 million liability limit before buying commercial auto and business liability coverage, since the contract dictates the insurance.

Send 25 or more applications a day with same-day follow-up calls, set keyword alerts on Indeed, CB Driver and Google, call department lines 9 to 11 a.m. Tuesday or Wednesday, and mine sam.gov for VA courier awards.
Charge a $35 minimum per pickup or a $750 to $1,000 weekly retainer and negotiate weekend, after-hour and wait-time terms with lab directors and pharmacy managers.
Write the client's stated volume assumptions into the bid, add pay-the-remainder cancellation language, and check deadhead miles, waiting time, stop count, exclusivity and equipment before signing.
Bank three months of operating expenses for 90-day first checks, then hire a driver only when $300 to $500 a week remains after driver pay and the contract allows subcontractors.
